question: B20 stamp ambiguity: slice 12 defines 'last boundary' as the step a boundary commit ENDED (Norn-Step of the commit with Norn-Outcome; a story at review shows 'last boundary: implement'). Stamping a non-holder's local-policy receipt with that step makes the holder (already at the next step) reject every answer/approval, and the restored human.test mailbox block (approve at the review#3 gate, then import -> $done) cannot pass. Which do you want? (a) stamp the step the last boundary LED TO, recorded by a new S4 trailer 'Norn-Next: <to-step>' on every boundary commit (golden/transcripts regenerated; reply: 'sent to X; the holder checks it against the step it is at (last boundary: implement -> review)'); (b) same but derive the to-step from the branch's workflow file (no new trailer, but wrong if the workflow file changed since the round was pinned); (c) literal: stamp the ended step (non-holder answers under local always rejected; the restored test then expects the rejection + Check item instead of $done).
